tasks.short: Improve health service delivery for target populations

steps.what: Design service delivery changes around population needs and practical constraints
Implement agreed service changes with delivery teams
Evaluate service effects, access and unintended consequences

tasks.design: Retain population-focused service design, implementation leadership and evaluation. Existing evidence in {DOCS} and coordination in {PROJECT} support the work; no general model is given service-allocation or evaluation authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service changes depend on local needs, resources and working relationships.
tasks.enabler_now: Generating a service proposal does not establish a feasible or effective delivery system.
tasks.still_hard: Access barriers, implementation effects and unintended consequences need local interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The physician connects population needs with workable clinical delivery and challenges simplistic measures.
tasks.altitude: Service design and evaluation responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Test feasibility of a proposed service change

evidence.claim: Retaining contextual service design and implementation leadership is an E1 assessment from model knowledge; the digest supplies no applicable measured automation case.

assumptions: Boundary is the physician's design, coordination and evaluation work, not the whole delivery team's effort.

Between s1 and s2, existing service leadership and clinical governance agree the design under current authority. Their unchanged decision work is outside this focal baseline, with no new transfer or saving claimed.
Service teams produce observations and feedback through existing delivery. No free structured access score or automated effectiveness label is assumed.
No custom software is proposed; existing document and project facilities remain. Zero upkeep because this design introduces no workflow change.
unknowns: Target population, decision rights and local service arrangements
research_questions: Which service change can be evaluated with meaningful access and health measures without assuming causation from activity counts?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Design, implementation and scientific evaluation retain their time; no unobserved administrative baseline is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and implement behavioural disease-prevention interventions

steps.what: Assess behavioural contributors and barriers with the affected population
Develop or implement interventions and adapt delivery with prevention partners

tasks.design: Keep assessment, intervention design and delivery decisions with the physician and prevention partners. Evidence in {DOCS} supports discussion; no system infers individual behavioural causes or sends targeted advice automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Behavioural interventions depend on practical circumstances and participant trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Generating persuasive text does not establish an effective or acceptable intervention.
tasks.still_hard: Behaviour reflects constraints as well as individual choice, and effects vary across groups.
tasks.human_edge: The physician recognises contextual barriers and adapts delivery without overstating causal claims.
tasks.altitude: Intervention responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify delivery barriers from participant feedback

evidence.claim: Keeping contextual behavioural-intervention work human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is the physician's intervention assessment and implementation contribution; publication of leaflets is separate work if present.
No structured behavioural profile, causal label or automatic targeting input is assumed.
Existing evidence and partner communication suffice; no custom tool is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no process change is introduced.
unknowns: Intervention type, population involvement and partner responsibilities
research_questions: Which contextual barriers would make a proposed behavioural intervention ineffective or unacceptable?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Contextual design and implementation retain all time; no guessed copywriting share is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Deliver presentations to public or professional audiences

steps.what: Deliver presentations and answer audience questions about preventive health

tasks.design: Retain live presentation and audience discussion with the physician. Existing material in {DOCS} supports delivery; creating slides is outside this task's delivery boundary.
tasks.previous_blocker: Live explanation depends on the audience's questions and understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Text or slide generation does not remove the presentation encounter.
tasks.still_hard: Technical uncertainty must be communicated clearly without misleading reassurance.
tasks.human_edge: The physician adapts explanations and responds to unexpected questions.
tasks.altitude: Presentation delivery and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Adapt spoken explanations to audience understanding

evidence.claim: Keeping live preventive-health presentations human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is delivery and questions, not slide writing or event logistics.
No machine action or free structured audience classification is assumed.
Existing presentation facilities remain; no custom build is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no task change is introduced.
research_questions: Which audience questions reveal misunderstandings requiring clearer explanation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Live delivery remains counted; preparation savings cannot be inferred from this task statement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain population-focused design, implementation leadership and live explanation; this batch establishes no removable clerical component.
reach: Interpret delivery barriers with community health workers
role.ambitious_version: A preventive physician who involves affected communities and tests whether service changes improve meaningful health and access outcomes.
